paper.title: AutoSkill: Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning via Skill Self-Evolution
paper.central_claim: AutoSkill extracts, maintains and reuses explicit versioned skills from interaction experience, enabling training-free lifelong personalized response improvement and portable skills across agents/users/tasks.

provenance.notes: sonnet slot configured as gpt-6.1-sol per dispatch; independently verifiable model receipt/session ID unavailable, no probe.

sections_read: Two §5.3 cases and all four post-conclusion skill examples

evidence.quote: To focus on interactions that contain sufficient context for stable skill induction, we retain only conversations with more than 8 turns.

evidence.quote: To illustrate how AutoSkill transforms interaction experience into explicit and reusable artifacts, we present two representative case studies drawn from the extracted SkillBank: one Chinese skill and one English skill.
evidence.support_explanation: Qualitative existing skill examples rather than controlled response outcomes.

evidence.quote: indicating that it has been iteratively refined 34 times through subsequent interaction experience.
evidence.support_explanation: Version 0.1.34 documents iterations; version count alone does not show quality gain.

evidence.quote: AutoSkill builds on the insight that retrieval can reactivate useful past experience, but it moves beyond conventional memory systems by lifting memory from text records to behavior units.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors position relative to Mem0/A-MEM/MemInsight; independent closest-neighbor texts absent.

evidence.quote: This design separates the latency-critical serving path from the learning path: retrieval and response generation remain on the critical path for the current request, while skill extraction and maintenance proceed concurrently as asynchronous background operations.
evidence.support_explanation: Asynchrony is architectural, not measured cost or latency.

signatures.information: User-query history and recent constraints; model responses excluded as extraction evidence; no downstream success labels.
signatures.operation: LLM extracts durable portable behavior; hybrid-retrieves neighbor; judge add/merge/discard; semantic-union merge preserving skill identity with version bump.
signatures.conditions: Durability judged correctly; user correction reflects stable preference rather than one-off request.
signatures.feedback: User requirements and corrections, not autonomous executable fitness
signatures.selection_rule: Prompted quality/coverage judge, no counterfactual task-gain gate
signatures.selection_data: User-query stream or filtered WildChat histories
signatures.persistence: SkillBank/Users/<user_id>/... and Common/... plus vector cache; version field updated.
signatures.later_use: Rewrite request, dense+BM25 thresholded Top-K; render relevant skills into future response prompt; no-match returns ordinary generation.
signatures.claimed_effect: Reusable personalized capability without weight changes.
signatures.failure_boundary: No response-quality evaluation; semantic gate may preserve bad rules; no measured retirement/regression protocol.

gap.author_gap: Memory stores text but does not operationalize durable personal behavior into explicit maintainable skills.
